title: Measurement: after an interrupt on a loaded Windows runner, a launcher descendant was still running when the supervisor returned
summary: F130, against ACC-0081. The focused Windows batch was CI run 36074016941 on the never-merged branch diag/f130-batch, after O1 (ca476de). It ran the full suite 8 times on windows-latest, 4 on Node 22 and 4 on Node 24. INTERRUPT MODE FAILED ONCE. In job 107881093769 (Node 24), test/shutdown-evidence.test.mjs's interrupt cell went like this. The launcher tree waited 4,226 ms for a descendant that did not exit. Its identity read was then allowed 2,225 ms, and the process table took 2,435 ms to its first byte, so the read was abandoned at 7,735 ms of the 8,000 ms budget. The supervisor returned shutdown-not-observed with launcher-descendants-unverified. It sent that pid nothing, because it could not verify the pid's identity, and that fail-closed report is correct. But the descendant, pid 5700, was STILL RUNNING when the supervisor returned, as the test's aliveAtReturn observation records. So both trees were not stopped, which ACC-0081 requires after an interrupt. ALSO OBSERVED AND OPEN. ACC-0116's real launch reported 'Not observed: agent-descendants' in 3 of 8 jobs. The piped Pi lives for about 1 to 2 seconds, and the Windows tracker samples every 3,000 ms with reads of 0.4 to 2.4 s, so no clean look completes while the agent is alive. WHAT O1 DID FIX. Natural-mode platform evidence passed 8 of 8, after 3 failures earlier on 2026-09-24. O1 is verified for natural shutdown only.
